verdict.root_cause: The failing hop is frontend->checkout PlaceOrder: traces show that gRPC call consuming 100% of trace time (18.4s, 24.0s, 52.7s) as pure self time with no corresponding checkout server span, while the ingress deadline cut at 15s [tr_6ef0d6740cf9]. Checkout's own downstream fan-out (cart, product-catalog, payment, shipping, email, currency, flagd) completes in tens of milliseconds in those same traces, and every currency call is answered in single-digit ms, so currency is not the culprit despite alerting first [tr_6ef0d6740cf9]. Checkout's error ratio rose ~26x with a change point at 22:51:31Z and a wide spread consistent with intermittent bursts [tr_e15b112d18b2], and no deploy, image swap, config push or flag edit is recorded for checkout, currency or their one-hop neighbours over 24h [tr_4120a3f3bc24, tr_5ee898a674ba]. The pattern - callers hanging to their deadline against a peer whose requests sometimes never produce a server span, with no change record anywhere - points at checkout accepting connections it does not serve: a stalled/frozen checkout process. Downstream services (payment, shipping, email, quote, accounting) alerted a minute later by starvation, not fault.
verdict.reasoning: Triage seeded on currency, but all three currency dispatches are either empty or exculpatory: no changes [tr_5ee898a674ba], no span-metric series in either window so the gap predates the incident and is an instrumentation gap rather than onset [tr_40d57e02ea67], no logs at all [tr_19bfe26748dc], and fast, error-free, fully-paired server spans [tr_6ef0d6740cf9]. The degradation localises one hop upstream of currency, at frontend->checkout, where the caller span is all self time with no attached checkout server span and the request dies at the 15s ingress deadline [tr_6ef0d6740cf9] - the hang-and-cascade shape in which errors surface at the proxy and everything behind the stuck caller goes quiet, matching the 23:20:31 cohort of downstream alerts. Checkout's measured error elevation and its early change point confirm checkout is genuinely misbehaving rather than merely reporting [tr_e15b112d18b2]. The empty change log across checkout and neighbours removes bad_deploy and bad_config as mechanisms [tr_4120a3f3bc24]. Process state rather than change makes restart_service the appropriate action. Confidence is low because no checkout-side logs, pod events or resource metrics were ever dispatched, and the freeze/partition distinction rests entirely on that missing evidence.
open_questions: No log query was run against checkout - its own log is the only thing that separates process_freeze (silent) from network_partition (repeating telemetry-export deadline lines) and from disk_fill (no space left on device).
Checkout's error ratio was intermittent with a change point at 22:51:31Z, ~28 minutes before the 23:19:31 alert; nothing explains that lead time or whether the two are the same fault.
No memory, CPU or container-restart data was gathered for checkout, so a memory squeeze producing stalls remains untested.
Both change-history queries returned empty; whether the change log itself is healthy was never verified, so a flag flip or unrecorded edit cannot be excluded.

alternatives.root_cause: Checkout's container is cut from its network, so callers hang on dropped packets while the process keeps running.
alternatives.why_not: Indistinguishable from a freeze at the caller, and the traces do show the hang shape - but two short traces show PlaceOrder failing fast with frontend dns.lookup and tcp.connect spans present [tr_6ef0d6740cf9], and checkout's own downstream calls to cart, payment and shipping succeed in the same traces, which a fully partitioned checkout could not do. Also unperformable: reconnect_service is not built.

alternatives.root_cause: Checkout is being squeezed against a container memory limit, stalling its request handlers intermittently.
alternatives.why_not: Fits the intermittent bursty error pattern [tr_e15b112d18b2], but no resource metric, container log or OOM signature was collected for checkout at all, and an empty change log [tr_4120a3f3bc24] leaves no recorded limit edit to revert; this is speculation where the freeze reading at least has trace-shaped support.

proposal.expected_effect: PlaceOrder traces regain a checkout server span and drop from 18-53s of pure self time to the tens-of-ms its fan-out already shows; frontend-proxy stops cutting at the 15s deadline; checkout's error ratio falls back toward its ~0.0009 baseline. Expect a thundering-herd error spike on checkout and its callers ~2 min after recreate, self-clearing within ~3; judge at the 10-minute mark.
proposal.if_wrong: PlaceOrder spans still show caller self time to the deadline with no checkout server span after ~10 minutes, or checkout's error ratio stays elevated past the herd window. That would point at a memory squeeze (restart returns under the same limit, fault recurs within minutes) or a network partition (fix is reconnect, which this executor cannot perform). Neither was tested: no checkout log query, no memory/CPU/restart-count data.
proposal.risk: Confidence is low and the discriminating evidence - checkout's own log - was never read. If this is resource_exhaustion the restart masks it briefly and it returns; if network_partition the recreate may or may not re-attach the container and we lose the frozen process state that would have identified the real mechanism. The action is irreversible and discards checkout's in-process cache.
proposal.blast_radius: checkout only, for the recreate duration. Its caller frontend (and frontend-proxy ingress behind it) sees connection resets; shipping, payment, email, quote, accounting see a brief further gap before traffic resumes.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Seven services alerting simultaneously at critical with a two-wave onset and no open incident to attribute it to; this cannot be dismissed. The fan-out across currency, payment, shipping and the proxy suggests a shared dependency or change, but nothing in the alerts picks a mechanism yet.
